issues.title: [Epic · Week 1] Product contracts and synthetic-development gate
issues.outcome: Approve the minimum product, architecture, legal, and synthetic-data contracts needed to begin foundation and UI work without waiting for Arcaea publication authorization.
scope: Own the phase dependency order.
Separate pre-authorization development from publication approval.
Close only with evidence.
acceptanceCriteria: Every open child issue has an owner and verifiable acceptance criteria.
Synthetic-only development boundaries are explicit.
Week 2 foundation can start without real Arcaea data or media.
Publication blockers remain represented by later release gates.
definitionOfDone: Acceptance criteria are verified.
Relevant documentation and tests are updated.
No unreviewed legal, accessibility, security, performance, privacy, or publication exception is introduced.

issues.title: [Week 1 · Data] Approve static catalog and replaceable data-adapter contract
issues.outcome: Choose a static, versioned catalog architecture whose UI can run on synthetic data now and switch to a permission-approved Arcaea source later without page rewrites.
scope: Define normalized domain boundaries, stable IDs, catalog manifest/version fields, and generated view models.
Define a `CatalogRepository` or equivalent adapter boundary with synthetic and future approved-source implementations.
Define build-time validation, browser loading, caching, stale/corrupt states, and rollback.
Record measured triggers for a hosted API or database; do not add one speculatively.
technicalConstraints: The approved source may later be a file export, API, repository, or database adapter; the UI contract must not assume which one.
Raw reviewed records remain separate from generated route indexes and view models.
acceptanceCriteria: ADR selects static versioned artifacts for the MVP.
Synthetic and future approved data sources satisfy the same application-facing interface.
Route components do not import raw catalog files or depend on an unknown lowiro API/database shape.
Failure and compatibility behavior is testable.
No backend is required for the synthetic preview.
definitionOfDone: Acceptance criteria are verified.
Relevant documentation and tests are updated.
No unreviewed legal, accessibility, security, performance, privacy, or publication exception is introduced.

issues.title: [Week 1 · Legal] Synthetic-development, provenance, and pre-permission guardrails
issues.outcome: Define what may be built and shown before lowiro authorization, how provenance/permission evidence will work later, and what remains blocked until written approval.
scope: Permit code, UI, schemas, tests, synthetic records, original prose, and project-authored neutral placeholders.
Prohibit real Arcaea catalog records, extracted resources, official media/text, copied community content, scraping, datamining, and public release claims before authorization.
Define source-record and asset-permission contracts for later approved integration.
Define synthetic-preview labeling, noindex expectations, correction/takedown path, and permission-request package.
Define the exact human approval points for contacting lowiro and activating release.
nonGoals: Do not request data before a representative synthetic prototype and publication scope exist.
Do not claim legal clearance or endorsement.
Do not implement the final real-data catalog in this issue.
acceptanceCriteria: Pre-authorization allowed and prohibited activities are unambiguous.
Synthetic records cannot be mistaken for Arcaea facts.
The permission package lists proposed fields, routes, branding, excluded content, hosting, provenance, and takedown controls.
Every future real fact group can reference sources and every future asset can reference permission evidence.
Silence is explicitly not treated as permission.
Public Arcaea-specific release remains blocked by `lowiro-publication-authorization` and `public-release-activation`.
definitionOfDone: Acceptance criteria are verified.
Relevant documentation and tests are updated.
No unreviewed legal, accessibility, security, performance, privacy, or publication exception is introduced.

issues.title: [Week 1 · Data] Define generic metadata schemas and synthetic seed catalog
issues.outcome: Define normalized, domain-capable schemas and a synthetic seed catalog that exercises every planned page without using Arcaea facts, names, prose, charts, or media.
scope: Schemas for songs, charts/difficulties, collections, characters, story entries, topics, releases, sources, assets, and catalog manifests.
Stable IDs, cross-entity references, unknown/review states, and version applicability.
Synthetic seed data and project-authored placeholder assets.
Validation rules, size limits, and generated application types.
nonGoals: Do not encode speculative fields solely because Sekai Viewer exposes them.
Do not import community databases or game dumps.
acceptanceCriteria: Schemas reject missing IDs, broken references, invalid URLs, duplicate keys, and unreviewed assets.
Seed records are clearly marked synthetic and do not resemble real Arcaea content.
Seed data exercises every MVP page template and failure state.
No protected chart, audio, image, story text, or extracted identifier is required.
The schema can later map permission-approved Arcaea records without changing page contracts.
definitionOfDone: Acceptance criteria are verified.
Relevant documentation and tests are updated.
No unreviewed legal, accessibility, security, performance, privacy, or publication exception is introduced.
